findings.issue: Number() coercion in PUT /reviews/:id/rating accepts non-numeric types that coerce into integers 1-5 (e.g. boolean true, single-element arrays), passing the Number.isInteger/range check and writing a corrupted rating value instead of rejecting the malformed request.
findings.evidence: const rating = Number(req.body.rating); if (!Number.isInteger(rating) || (rating < 1 || rating > 5)) {...} — Number(true) === 1 and Number([4]) === 4, both pass validation and get persisted via Review.updateReview(reviewId, { rating }).

findings.issue: page=0 (and pageSize=0) in GET /books/page is silently coerced to the default (1 / 10) via `|| 1` / `|| 10` before the `page < 1 || pageSize < 1` check runs, so the documented 400 'page must be >= 1' validation never triggers for an explicit 0 value; the endpoint instead returns 200 with default-page results.
findings.evidence: const page = parseInt(req.query.page as string, 10) || 1; const pageSize = parseInt(req.query.pageSize as string, 10) || 10; if (page < 1 || pageSize < 1 || pageSize > 100) { return res.status(400)... } — parseInt('0',10) is 0, which is falsy, so `0 || 1` becomes 1 before the bounds check runs.
